center.locator: Arithmetic mean of the 53 vertices of the merged KEKB/SuperKEKB ring (OSM way 138322704)
center.note: Map centre only; not a claim about any structure. precision_m is set loosely because this is a naive vertex-average centroid, not an area centroid.

levels.note: The ring is commonly described as roughly 11 m underground, but no official page fetched this session states a metre figure, so depth_m is left null per A17 rather than guessed.

accelerator:kek-ps is drawn (geometry:kek-north-counter-hall) rather than listed in `unlocated[]`, but with an explicitly flagged, circumstantial identification -- see that record's own notes and the worklog's 'Conflicts and honesty calls' section. No source found this session gives the 12 GeV PS ring's own tunnel path; two targeted Overpass searches for tunnel/particle_accelerator/landuse ways near the historic PS site found none.

summary.plain: KEK's Tsukuba campus, Japan's oldest national particle-physics laboratory: the three-kilometre KEKB/SuperKEKB collider ring that has driven the Belle and Belle II experiments since 1998, and the site of the historic 12 GeV proton synchrotron that drove the world's first long-baseline accelerator neutrino beam, K2K.
summary.technical: One local map for facility:kek covering the Tsukuba campus: the 3016 m KEKB/SuperKEKB ring tunnel (OSM way 138322704, cross-checked against the SuperKEKB accelerator paper's own machine-parameter table), the Tsukuba interaction hall (Belle, Belle II) and the ring's Oho/Fuji/Nikko straight-section halls, the KEK injector linac building, a building tentatively identified with the historic KEK-PS North Counter Hall, and an inferred-direction line for the K2K beam toward Super-Kamiokande.
